subject: MARI_PERFORMANCE_TRANSFER_v1

renderer.channel: cross-speaker --emo-ref acoustic prefix while retaining Mari x-vector

references.attribution: AMI Meeting Corpus, University of Edinburgh, https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/corpus/
references.selection_rule: one deterministic medium-length lexical dialogue act per A/B/D; no Mari-similarity or output-quality selection

donors.text: so um fish was a natural choice .
Do you want to introduce yourself again ?

verification.reason: all six donor-conditioned outputs failed Mari speaker-identity admission

targets.text: I don't think that's right. Give me a second. The keys are in the kitchen, not the car.
I noticed. I just wasn't going to make a thing out of it unless you asked.

established: The native cross-speaker acoustic-reference route has strong acoustic consequence.
Target lexical intelligibility can remain high under that conditioning.
Supplying Mari's frozen x-vector does not prevent the acoustic-reference route from strongly changing speaker identity.
The current --emo-ref route is too speaker-entangled to serve as identity-safe performance transfer.
not_established: Whether any failed conditioned clip has better acting or conversational believability.
Whether performance transfer as a general concept is impossible.
Whether a speaker-invariant or explicitly disentangled performance representation would fail.

decision.next_architecture_candidate: extract/learn speaker-invariant performance representation across multiple human speakers, then condition Mari through a channel explicitly orthogonalized against speaker identity rather than raw acoustic prefix conditioning

proof_ceiling: This experiment rejects this specific raw cross-speaker acoustic-prefix route for Mari performance transfer. It does not reject the broader goal of transferring performance separately from speaker identity.
